main_text.l: deniq; vbique locorum πολυπραγμονέιν, & lunonium incedere & sefe venditare debere, significem, eiusmodi enim Magistros noftros, in Togafalcantis perfonam induce-te, nihilo prestantiores esse autumo: Sed vt auri precium & sincerirtas, de recta S. Theologiae aestimatione, hieroglyphice te admonear. Scis enim doctrinam diuinitus patefactam auro obryzo pretiosiorem esse: scis etiam, ἀλληφθέγματι doctrinae coelestis summa esse, eoq; nomine studiosissime nobis retinendam: Ideo tui muneris erit, profes-sionem sanç doctrinae constanter retinere, & omnibus totius Mundi opibus antepo-nere. Semper ergo repetes illos dulces verſiculos de doctrina Christi.
Erit etiam tibi hic anulus, arrhabo τῆς φιλαληθείας καὶ φιλαδελφίας, de quibus praecla-re dixit Zacharias Propheta: Diligite veri-tatem & pacem cap. 8. 19.

Quartò, Pileum capiti tuo impono, non vt multis agam de dignitate & priuilegio terreno, quale fuit eorum, qui νομοφύλακες καὶ ἱεροφάντορες dicebantur, & in theatro vt-bis Atticae loco sublimi, fasci-js cādidis, honoris causfa, ornati, sedebant: sed vt de libe-ra veri-

page.notes: Greek text in the epigram and in the Greek words of the paragraphs is reproduced from a low-resolution scan and is uncertain in places; the epigram lines and some accents may not be exact. The line "ra veri-" at the foot is a catchword-like fragment of a split word and is kept as the last line of text. The Latin word "ἀλληφθέγματι" is a best reading of a damaged Greek word. The marginal "t" beside the text near "nihilo" is a printed mark, not a note. Several words in the scan (e.g. "Scis", "sincerirtas", "prestantiores") are read with some doubt.
